description: Render a new clip FROM the motion of an existing one: your reference clip leads (camera move, blocking, timing), the model restyles what happens in it. Pass the clip's URL directly — the one you already have from lab_list_assets (asset_type 'video'), lab_job_status or lab_review_queue; nothing is looked up. Reference images bind cast, place and look; in_sec/out_sec cut the reference server-side before it ever reaches the provider, so you pay for the excerpt, not the source. Same backend path as lab_animate's source_video_id, with the fields that only exist there. Costs credits when called without get_cost. WITHOUT a reference clip (leave reference_video_url out), the images and sounds in `referenzen` alone guide the run — only for models whose lab_list_models entry says referenzen_ohne_video: true, and only FACELESS references (ort, stil, bild, stimme, ton): Seedance 2.5 rejects faces as reference images, even invented characters (measured 2026-09-27), so `figur` is refused before anything is charged. For a person, build a still with them first and animate it with lab_animate. Name the references in the prompt as 'reference only, never shown on screen', and avoid the word 'static' for short shots — it tends to return frozen frames.

aspect_ratio.description: Output aspect ratio on this path, written as width:height or 'auto'. Only models whose lab_list_models entry takes it on the reference path accept it; for any other model the backend refuses it before anything is charged, and the refusal lists the allowed values. Omitted, the model's fixed default applies.

character_ref_urls.description: Ready image URLs that bind the cast's identity. The name says URLs on purpose: lab_animate's `character_refs` takes character sheet IDS, this path takes ADDRESSES, and the two are not interchangeable. Get them from lab_get_character_sheet. Omit to let the backend use the project's world-bible characters. Mutually exclusive with `referenzen`.

duration_seconds.description: Length of the NEW clip. Must lie inside the chosen model's duration grid from lab_list_models — the per-model ceiling is enforced by the backend and rejected rather than silently clamped.

first_frame_url.description: Guiding frame for the START of the new clip (image URL). Only the wan_vace path binds guiding frames to the provider — with any other model the backend REJECTS this field instead of swallowing it, because a swallowed guiding frame means paying for a run identical to the one without it.

generate_audio.description: Let the model generate sound with the clip — only models whose lab_list_models entry can output audio take it on this path. Omitted = no generated sound. Generated audio REPLACES any voice in the reference — to keep a spoken take, leave it off.

get_cost.description: Preflight: return the price in credits and your balance WITHOUT generating and without spending anything, reading the same catalog as lab_list_models. Do this before a long take or when the user should confirm the cost.

in_sec.description: Cut the reference clip server-side before it reaches the provider: start of the excerpt, in seconds from the clip's beginning. Only together with out_sec.

kamerapfad.description: The camera move as INPUT instead of prose: an object following shared/kamerapfad/schema.json — poses over time (position, look-at or quaternion, metres, Y up) from the Kadrage terrain flight or drawn by hand, or motion phases as lab_kamerafahrt reads them from a clip (its answer carries a ready `kamerapfad`). The backend validates it, derives phases, and adds the move as a paragraph after your prompt, before the reference markers (the reference clip still leads the motion as the first video reference). WHICH FORM that paragraph takes depends on the model: prose for most families, bracketed director commands for the MiniMax/Hailuo family, which parses them. NO MODEL RECEIVES THE POSES TODAY — the answer says which form went out (kamerapfad.angewandt = als_text or als_regiebefehle), names the family rule and the source it rests on (kamerapfad.sprache), and lists what that form could not carry. If your own prompt already carries bracketed commands, the path is NOT sent on top of them (angewandt = eigene_regie, with kamerapfad.eigene_regiebefehle naming what it found). A `zusammenfassung` inside the path is display only and is NEVER sent — the move is always rebuilt from the phases; if nothing can be built, the answer says angewandt = nicht_ableitbar with the reason, and nothing of the path is in the prompt. Mutually exclusive with kamerapfad_url.

kamerapfad_url.description: Address of a kamerapfad JSON instead of the object — the url of a file in THIS project (lab_list_assets), e.g. the kamerapfad JSON that Kadrage writes next to its flight video. Fetched by the backend under the same ownership rule as every reference: a file of another project is a named rejection before anything is charged. Mutually exclusive with kamerapfad.

last_frame_url.description: Guiding frame for the END of the new clip (image URL). Same rule as first_frame_url: wan_vace only, rejected elsewhere rather than dropped.

out_sec.description: End of the excerpt in the reference clip, in seconds. Must lie behind in_sec; both are set together or neither.

project_id.description: Project id (from lab_list_projects) — positive integer as string. On this path it travels in the request BODY, not in the URL, but it is just as required: the new clip is filed under this project.

prompt.description: What the new clip should show. Describe it — do NOT phrase it as an instruction to edit or extend the reference; some models classify the run by the verb and then reject the aspect ratio and duration after queueing.

reference_video_url.description: URL of the clip whose motion is taken. Use the url/video_url a previous answer gave you (lab_list_assets with asset_type 'video', lab_job_status, lab_review_queue) — never a hand-built address: the bucket is not guessable and a wrong one renders and bills into a 404. Leave it out to run on `referenzen` alone (at least one image reference, no `figur`, no in_sec/out_sec, no depth) — the models that allow it carry referenzen_ohne_video in lab_list_models.

referenzen.description: The typed successor of character_ref_urls: each reference says WHAT it is, so a place or a look no longer has to travel disguised as a character. Since 2026-09-03 it carries all three channels, not just images: motion references ride alongside the reference clip, sound references go into the model's audio slots. The position IS the address — the images are @Image1..n, the reference clip is @Video1 and the extra motion references follow it, the sounds are @Audio1..n. Image references are MEASURED before they are sent and scaled up to the model's minimum if they fall below it; a reference is never rejected for being small. Mutually exclusive with character_ref_urls — two sources for one list means one of them silently loses. What a model takes per channel is in lab_list_models (referenz_grenzen).

art.description: What this reference IS: figur a character, ort a place, stil a look, motion a movement, raum a spatial/white-model pass, stimme a voice, clay an untextured geometry render, kreativ a free creative reference. The last three say only the CHANNEL, for when the role is not the point: bild any image, video any clip, ton any sound. Not every class has a slot on every model, and which ones do changes as models land: the backend answers a class it cannot route with a named rejection that says why, instead of accepting the reference and quietly ignoring it. Nothing is charged for such a rejection.

rolle.description: WHICH character or place this reference means. Free text, carried through — it is not derivable from `art`, and guessing it would be a claim about the cast nobody made.

url.description: URL of the reference — an image, a clip or a sound file, matching `art`

resolution.description: Render resolution on this path, copied verbatim from the model's resolutions in lab_list_models. The run is priced at the resolution you choose — the low tier costs a fraction of the default — so pass it for sound-only or test runs. Omitted, the model's default applies.

task.description: reference (default): the references guide a new clip. editing: the picture of the reference clip stays and only what the prompt names changes — e.g. 'keep the picture, generate matching sound effects, no music' with generate_audio: true. Needs a reference clip. Edit verbs in the prompt are expected here, not refused.

ton.description: Which sound the result carries. quelle: the reference clip's own audio is laid back under the new picture after generation — the way to keep a spoken take, since models that regenerate audio replace the voice. generiert: keep the model's sound (needs generate_audio: true). keiner: no sound. Omitted: quelle when a reference clip is given and generate_audio is off, generiert when generate_audio is on, keiner otherwise. The finished run reports in metadata what actually lies underneath (ton) and how far picture and sound differ in length (ton_drift_s).

tool.description: Video model id — copy it verbatim from lab_list_models (kind: video), and only models the catalog marks v2v take a reference clip at all. Omit to let the backend use its own default for this path. Durations, resolutions and price live in the catalog, this text names none.

use_depth.description: Condition the run on a depth pass of the reference clip. Defaults to ON in the backend; pass false to opt out. Models that do not have a depth stage ignore it — the answer says so rather than pretending it happened. To RE-FILM a take from new camera angles, pass false: a depth pass locks the geometry of the reference, and the new angles cannot happen. task='editing' ignores it anyway.

wechsel_von.description: The model id this call switches AWAY from (as listed in lab_list_models), with the same references as before. The answer then carries `wechsel`: which references the switch cuts off and why, and which ones the new model picks up. Nothing is sent to the old model; the field only names the comparison.

name: lab_reference_motion
title: Motion from a Clip
